analysis.title: Tyler Technologies Inc. (TYL) 3Q26: Cloud positioned to accelerate in 2027; AI contributions further out
key_insights: GS maintains Neutral on TYL and raises the 12-month price target to $385 from $345, based on 32x SNTM (Q5-Q8) GAAP EPS (vs 30x prior), mainly reflecting peer multiple expansion. Price is $394.30, implying 2.4% downside.
TYL rose 4% on 10/29 after 3Q results (NASDAQ -1%). Revenue was 0.6% below the Street, EBIT margins were in line, and FY26 guidance was lowered at the high end.

GS attributes the stock reaction to TYL's position as an idiosyncratic hedge to the AI ecosystem, plus on-premise customer engagement ahead of an expected cloud migration acceleration in 2027 and early AI traction.

Cloud transition is progressing but conversion timing is uneven. Management has become more proactive after its July outreach to on-premise Enterprise customers, with direct sales engagement, migration pricing strategies, and the start of end-of-life announcements for on-premise support and product upgrades.
Tyler expects migrations to accelerate in 2027 and completed its first live implementation of the multi-tenant Cloud Living model in 3Q, with broader rollouts expected in 2027.
Total SaaS bookings grew 14% in 3Q versus 21% in 2Q.
Tyler closed about 300 deals containing AI solutions YTD, about 130 of them in 3Q, with the price uplift on these deals still in the low single digits.

Customers favor embedded AI functionality over standalone solutions, and adoption is strongest where ROI is readily measurable. Tyler has 11 agents and assistants generally available and plans 25 by year-end.
Management does not expect meaningful revenue contribution from newer agentic capabilities until at least 2H27. GS sees AI near term as a cloud migration and product differentiation driver.
GS prefers to own stocks with more immediate AI catalysts into 2027, while noting Tyler is moving at an appropriate pace for its customer base.
3Q26 total revenue was $648mn versus GSe $658mn and Street $651mn (-1.6% vs GSe, -0.6% vs Street), up 9% y/y. EPS was $3.52 versus GSe $3.51 and Street $3.49.
3Q26 SaaS revenue was $242mn (+21% y/y), transaction-based revenue $220mn (+9% y/y), and professional services revenue $63mn (-3% y/y, 5.1% below GSe). Free cash flow was $277mn, 15.8% above Street.

market_movers.rationale: PT raised from $345 to $385 on a higher target multiple of 32x SNTM GAAP EPS (vs 30x), reflecting peer multiple expansion. Rating stays Neutral with 2.4% downside to the current price.

sector_views.rationale: GS prefers software stocks with more immediate AI catalysts into 2027 over TYL, whose AI revenue contribution is expected from 2H27 at the earliest.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported EPS $3.52 vs GSe $3.51 and Street (Visible Alpha) $3.49, up 18% y/y. Already reported on 10/29.

3Q26 reported total revenue $648mn vs GSe $658mn and Street $651mn, up 9% y/y. Subscription revenue was $463mn (+15% y/y), maintenance revenue $106mn (-5% y/y), and other revenues $16mn (-16% y/y, 24.3% below GSe).
3Q26 reported operating income $182mn (28% margin) vs GSe $185mn and Street $180mn. Reported free cash flow was $277mn (43% margin) vs GSe $273mn and Street $239mn.
FY26 guidance was lowered at the high end, per Visible Alpha Consensus Data.
GS forecasts: next-quarter EPS 12/26E $3.43, 3/27E $3.48, 6/27E $3.80. Full-year EPS estimates are $13.10 (2026E), $15.21 (2027E), and $17.36 (2028E). These are GS estimates, not reported figures.
risk_factors: Downside risks: cross-sell execution issues across the broader suite, including payments, which could slow growth and worsen unit economics.
Changes in government budgets from changing regulations or spending priorities could weigh on growth.
Lower transaction volumes or an inability to raise payments pricing could hurt growth and margins.
Slower organic growth if government technology adoption slows after the COVID-driven adoption cycle.

Upside risks: faster cloud conversions, SaaS growth above the low-teens framework, transactions outperforming the ~10% framework, earlier AI monetization, faster margin expansion, M&A, and larger capital returns.
vol_and_positioning: TYL shares are up 22.0% over 3 months and 15.6% over 6 months, but down 17.5% over 12 months (25.8% behind the S&P 500). GS describes the stock as an idiosyncratic hedge to the AI ecosystem.

tension_points.bull_case: Management has become more proactive with on-premise Enterprise customers (direct sales, migration pricing, end-of-life dates), engagement is positive, and Tyler expects an accelerating pace of migrations in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Conversion timing remains uneven, total SaaS bookings slowed to +14% from +21% in 2Q, and FY26 guidance was lowered at the high end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Cloud conversions failing to accelerate in 2027 as management expects.
